main_body: A palm tree: a curved brown trunk with a drooping frond canopy at the top and two orange coconuts under the fronds.
top_band: none as a flat surface. The column at x=15 shows dark green outline (rows 2-4), light green (rows 5-6), then mid and dark green frond rows, then the brown trunk from row 11. These are leaf clumps, not a horizontal surface.
evidence: The object is an organic palm tree whose silhouette is a trunk with drooping fronds. It has no flat top surface and no box-like front face, so the 3/4 top-plus-front test does not apply in the usual way. The fronds do cover the top of the trunk and read as a volumetric canopy, with a light highlight at the upper rows and darker drooping fronds below. The trunk is drawn as a straight vertical column with no visible top, but it is hidden under the canopy. As an organic piece this is the normal way to draw a palm in this view. The canopy is small and sparse, so the 3/4 reading is weak, but nothing in it is a wrongly drawn horizontal surface.

style.evidence: The references are dense, round, many-clumped canopies with 108-109 colours per tile and 427-567 distinct colours. The candidate is a thin, sparse palm with only 15 distinct colours in total, although its median per tile is 10. The canopy shows about 3-4 greens (dark, mid, light, highlight) and the trunk about 3-4 browns. Outlines are tinted dark green and dark brown, which is good, and there are no flat 5x5 fills. But the colour count is far below the references, the canopy fronds are drawn as simple stripes with little clump texture, and the trunk is a plain banded column. It would look thinner and flatter than the Beodeul trees next to them.
